title: Block C DID resolution is fully serial — 16 distinct issuers force 16 sequential HTTPS round trips
rationale: Added resolveIssuersParallel (dedup + bounded goroutine pool via buffered channel semaphore of size 8 using stdlib sync.WaitGroup) and verifyJWTSignatureWithKey (network-free sibling). Block C now pre-resolves all unique issuer DIDs concurrently then verifies signatures from map. No new dependencies.
variants_checked: chain.go Block C receipt loop (line 236) and invocation verification (line 243) — both converted; original verifyJWTSignature preserved for future callers
bypass_considered: 16 distinct did:web issuers at 10s each: was 160s serial, now ceil(16/8)*10s=20s parallel. Context cancellation propagates to all goroutines via ctx
test_note: TestResolveIssuersParallelDeduplicates (5 DIDs with duplicates → 2 unique entries), TestBlockCResolvesAllDistinctIssuers (4-receipt/5-issuer chain end-to-end), TestResolveIssuersParallelContextCancellation added to chain_test.go
review_reason: The patch fixes the serial-blocking-IO root cause by lifting all DID resolutions out of the Block C loop into resolveIssuersParallel (bounded to 8 concurrent goroutines via semaphore). The resolvedKeys map is written sequentially after wg.Wait() closes the fully-buffered results channel — no data race. The fail-closed !ok check on missing DIDs preserves the security invariant. Note: original verifyJWTSignature is now dead code within Chain and should be cleaned up in a follow-up.
